'''Abraham Klein''' (January 10, 1927 &ndash; January 20, 2003) was an American [[theoretical physicist]]. 

Klein received his B.A. from [[Brooklyn College]] in 1947, and his S.M. (1948) and Ph.D. (1950) degrees from [[Harvard University]] under [[Julian Schwinger]]. In 1955, he became associate professor at the [[University of Pennsylvania]], achieving full professorship in 1958 and retiring in 1994.

Klein studied models of collective behavior in finite many-body systems, especially in [[nuclear physics]], for example in [[Boson]] model and in an extension of the [[Hartree–Fock method]] with Robert Kerman (Kerman–Klein method).<ref>{{cite journal
|author1=Arthur K. Kerman|author1-link=Arthur Kerman |author2=Abraham Klein |title=Generalized Hartree-Fock Approximation for the Calculation of Collective States of a Finite Many-Particle System
|journal=Physical Review
|doi=10.1103/PhysRev.132.1326
|year=1963
|volume=132
|issue=3
|pages=1326–1342
|bibcode = 1963PhRv..132.1326K }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
|author1=Abraham Klein |author2=Arthur K. Kerman |title=Collective motion in finite many particle states II
|journal=Physical Review
|doi=10.1103/PhysRev.138.B1323
|year=1965
|volume=138
|issue=5B
|pages=B1323–B1332
|bibcode = 1965PhRv..138.1323K }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
|author1=Abraham Klein |author2=Louis Celenza |author3=Arthur K. Kerman |title=Collective Motion in Finite Many-Particle Systems. III. Foundations of a Theory of Rotational Spectra of Deformed Nuclei.
|journal=Physical Review
|doi=10.1103/PhysRev.140.B245
|year=1965
|volume=140
|issue=2B
|pages=B245–B263
|bibcode = 1965PhRv..140..245K }}</ref> In the 1980s he occupied himself with, among other things, the [[interacting boson model]],<ref>{{cite journal
|author1=Abraham Klein |author2=Ching-Teh Li |author3=Michel Vallieres |title=Relationship between the Bohr-Mottelson model and the interacting boson model
|journal=Physical Review C
|doi=10.1103/PhysRevC.25.2733
|year=1982
|volume=25
|issue=5
|pages=2733–2742
|bibcode = 1982PhRvC..25.2733K }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
|author1=Abraham Klein |author2=Michel Vallieres |title=Relationship between the Bohr Collective Hamiltonian and the Interacting-Boson Model
|journal=Physical Review Letters
|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.46.586
|year=1981
|volume=46
|issue=9
|pages=586–590
|bibcode = 1981PhRvL..46..586K }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
|author1=Abraham Klein |author2=Ching-Teh Li |author3=Michel Vallieres |title=Relationship Between the Interacting Boson Model and the Bohr Collective Hamiltonian
|journal=Physica Scripta
|doi=10.1088/0031-8949/25/3/003
|year=1982
|volume=25
|issue=3
|pages=452–458
|bibcode = 1982PhyS...25..452K |s2cid=250833136 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
|author1=Abraham Klein |author2=Ching-Teh Li |author3=Thomas D. Cohen |author4=Michel Vallieres |title=Relationship Between the Interacting Boson Model and the Bohr Collective Hamiltonian
|journal=Progress in Particle and Nuclear Physics
|doi=10.1016/0146-6410(83)90018-2
|year=1983
|volume=9
|issue=
|pages=183–231
|bibcode = 1983PrPNP...9..183K }}</ref> and in the 1970s with [[quantum field theory]] in strong fields (with [[Johann Rafelski]]).

In 1964, Klein published an article about [[spontaneous symmetry breaking]] with his student [[Benjamin W. Lee]] and contributed to the appearance of [[Higgs mechanism]].<ref>{{cite journal |author1=A. Klein |author2=B.W. Lee |name-list-style=amp |year=1964 |title=Does Spontaneous Breakdown of Symmetry Imply Zero-Mass Particles? |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=12 |issue=10 |page=266 |bibcode=1964PhRvL..12..266K |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.12.266 |s2cid=15349102}}</ref>

He was a [[Sloan Fellow]] and [[Guggenheim Fellow]], Honorary Doctor of [[Goethe University of Frankfurt]], and Alexander von Humboldt Senior Scientist. Klein was a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].

He was married and had two daughters.
